byte-identical against the retail DOL by research/tools/matching-decomp/match.py.
Re-prove the whole file with:  python src-match/verify.py
`exact_bytes` false is NOT a weaker result: it means the object carries a
relocation whose operand field is legitimately zero before linking, and the
match was established on the relocation's SYMBOL instead. See zz_00122c8_.
`iterations` is the number of candidate C sources written before the oracle
returned MATCH. It is the number that sizes an LLM loop, and it is measured

compiler.fork_note: This project extends the pinned commit. `python research/tools/matching-decomp/mwcc_fork.py --check` says whether the checkout at .tools/mwcc-rs carries the changes; --apply installs them over a fresh extract of the pinned tarball, byte for byte. TOOLCHAIN.md section 5 lists what each change does and what it unlocks. Entries below marked `needs_fork` do NOT match on the unmodified pinned commit.

attempted_and_blocked.name: zz_0298b20_
attempted_and_blocked.blocker: register allocation: retail `mulli r0, r4, 0x74`, mwcc-rs `mulli r4, r4, 0x74`
attempted_and_blocked.detail: Retail routes the scaled array index through the scratch register r0; mwcc-rs reuses the dead input r4. Four different C spellings produced the same divergence, so it is not reachable from the source. mwcc-rs's own README names matching MWCC's register colouring as `the core research target`.
attempted_and_blocked.measured_2026_09_04: blocker_census.py --scaled-index, over all 12,062 functions: of the 7,085 mulli/slwi sites whose product feeds an address computation, 4,706 (66.4%) land in r0, 1,008 (14.2%) reuse the index register -- mwcc-rs's default -- and 1,371 (19.4%) take a third register. The default is the MINORITY choice. Forcing the one existing r0 preference in expressions/members.rs to GENERAL_SCRATCH, rebuilding and re-running changed nothing here, so this function's mulli comes from a different one of the ~40 scaling sites: it needs one register model for address temporaries, not a per-site preference. KNOWN CEILING -- a candidate differing only in which register holds a scaled index is not a bad candidate, and a loop must not iterate against it. See TOOLCHAIN.md section 5.3.
